facts.text: Brooklyn Heights began as part of Brooklyn Township; first permanent log cabin built in 1812 by James Fish near present Denison Ave.
The village grew into the "Greenhouse Center of America" with over 100 acres of glass‑covered vegetable farms by mid‑20th century.
In 1938, Brooklyn Heights joined the Cuyahoga Heights School District, marking a shift toward integrated education.
The Cleveland office of the National Weather Service sits in Brooklyn Heights, making it a key weather monitoring spot.
The southern edge of Brooklyn Heights features a heavily wooded valley with a creek cutting through, offering a natural green corridor.
Connecticut settlers, including the Fish family, arrived after the 1805 Treaty of Fort Industry cleared Native title, establishing the first organized occupation west of the Cuyahoga River.
